skill.name: ponytail-audit
skill.description: Reviews an entire repository for unnecessary complexity and ranks opportunities to delete code, simplify abstractions, or replace dependencies without applying changes.
skill.summary: Get a ranked repository complexity report with suggested replacements and estimated code and dependency reductions.
skill.author: dietrichgebert

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around category labels and output templates. SKILL.md requests a report without applying changes; no evidence found of command execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection. Its exclusion of security review defines the audit scope, not an instruction to bypass this assessment.

static_findings.snippet: - `delete:` dead code, unused flexibility, speculative feature. Replacement: nothing.
- `stdlib:` hand-rolled thing the standard library ships. Name the function.
- `native:` dependency or code doing what the platform already does. Name the feature.
- `yagni:` abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets, layer with one caller.
- `shrink:` same logic, fewer lines. Show the shorter form.
One line per finding, ranked: `<tag> <what to cut>. <replacement>. [path]`.
End with `net: -<N> lines, -<M> deps possible.` Nothing to cut: `Lean already. Ship.`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown backticks to format the delete category label. The surrounding prose defines a report category, not a shell command.
Line 20 formats the stdlib category label with Markdown backticks. It requests a standard library replacement recommendation and contains no execution instruction.
Line 21 uses Markdown backticks around the native category label. This describes platform replacement recommendations, not executable code or command substitution.
Line 22 formats the yagni category label with Markdown backticks. Its examples describe unnecessary abstractions without requesting command execution.
Line 23 uses Markdown backticks for the shrink category label. Showing a shorter form in a report does not execute it.
Line 33 formats a textual finding template with Markdown backticks. The placeholders define report output rather than an executable Ruby or shell expression.
Line 34 uses Markdown backticks around a reduction estimate and the response for no findings. Both are literal report text, not commands.

content.user_title: Audit Repository Complexity and Unnecessary Code
content.value_statement: Unnecessary abstractions and redundant dependencies make repositories harder to maintain. This skill reviews the whole codebase and ranks deletion, simplification, and replacement opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the whole repository rather than only a change diff.
Identifies dead code, unused configuration, single-implementation interfaces, and wrappers that only delegate.
Suggests standard library functions or platform features that could replace custom code or dependencies.
Groups findings into delete, stdlib, native, yagni, and shrink categories, ranked by the largest reduction first.
Produces concise findings with file paths and an estimate of possible line and dependency reductions.
limitations: Reports recommendations only; it does not apply fixes.
Correctness bugs, security vulnerabilities, and performance problems are outside its scope.
Suggested reductions are estimates, not measured or verified changes.
Review quality depends on repository access and the host assistant's available context.

use_cases.title: Plan Repository Cleanup
use_cases.description: Identify the largest opportunities to remove unnecessary abstractions before scheduling maintenance work.

use_cases.title: Reduce Dependency Overlap
use_cases.description: Review dependencies for functionality already available in the standard library or deployment platform.

use_cases.title: Assess an Inherited Codebase
use_cases.description: Get a ranked overview of dead configuration, redundant wrappers, and speculative flexibility in an unfamiliar repository.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Complexity Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run ponytail-audit on this repository. Rank unnecessary complexity by the largest potential reduction and do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dependency Replacements
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this whole repository for over-engineering. Highlight dependencies that standard library functions or native platform features could replace.

prompt_templates.title: Review Abstractions and Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Run ponytail-audit across the repository. Identify single-implementation interfaces, delegating wrappers, unused configuration, and speculative features. Rank findings by potential reduction.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Prioritized Cleanup Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the entire repository for complexity. Use category tags, replacements, and file paths. Rank largest reductions first and estimate total removable lines and dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare recommendations for a maintenance review.

output_examples.input: Audit a repository with a redundant wrapper and an unused configuration option.
output: Illustrative finding: remove the delegating wrapper and use its underlying implementation directly, with the relevant repository path.
Illustrative finding: remove the unused configuration option without a replacement, with the relevant repository path.
Finish with estimated removable lines and dependencies.

output_examples.input: Audit a repository where no unnecessary complexity is identified.

best_practices: Provide repository access and relevant platform constraints before requesting the audit.
Verify usage and compatibility before accepting a deletion or replacement recommendation.
Apply approved changes separately and run tests; use a normal review for correctness, security, and performance.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated reductions as guaranteed savings.
Deleting code solely because an abstraction has one implementation.
Using a complexity audit as a substitute for security or correctness review.

faq.question: Does this skill review the whole repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews the repository tree rather than only a change diff.

faq.question: Does it modify or delete files?
faq.answer: No. It produces a one-time report and does not apply fixes.

faq.question: What kinds of complexity does it identify?
faq.answer: It looks for dead code, redundant dependencies, unused configuration, unnecessary abstractions, and opportunities to shorten equivalent logic.

faq.question: Does it check security, correctness, or performance?
faq.answer: No. Those concerns are explicitly outside its scope and require a normal review.

faq.question: How are findings organized?
faq.answer: Findings use delete, stdlib, native, yagni, or shrink tags. Each includes a recommendation and path, ranked by the largest reduction first.

faq.question: How do I leave the audit mode?
faq.answer: Say "stop ponytail-audit" or "normal mode" to return to normal interaction.
